note: Original ten-block townsite (Aitkin plan). Front Street followed the shoreline; Adelaide was then Duke Street.

Not a town limit: the same plan set aside the land east of Parliament Street to the Don, and west of Peter Street to the Humber, for government and military purposes; all land south of Lot (Queen) Street was reserved.

Westward extension ('New Town'). York article: area west to Peter Street annexed in 1797; neighbourhoods article gives the New Town as Jarvis to Peter, south of Queen, north of Front (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_neighbourhoods_in_Toronto). The strip between George and Jarvis is not assigned by either source.

Built-up area about the time of incorporation: 'fully developed as far west as York Street, with some built-up areas west to Peter'; business district on King and Front from Yonge to the Don bridge; the original townsite itself not fully built. No north limit stated (Macaulaytown lay north of Lot Street, west of Yonge). Undated in the source: 1834 is the context ('by the time of incorporation').

City proper at incorporation, 6 March 1834. North limit: Old Toronto article says 400 yards north of Lot (Queen) Street; Amalgamation article says 'a line analogous to Dundas Street' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amalgamation_of_Toronto).
The liberties outside the city proper, 1834. Plus a strip along the lakeshore east of the Don, south of Queen Street, to about today's Maclean Avenue.
Liberties formally became part of the city in 1859 and the wards were remapped; same outer limits as 1834 (plus the lakeshore strip east of the Don). Boundaries then unchanged until 1883.

south: railway tracks and a line between Wright Avenue and Fern Avenue

note: Riverside, Don Mount and Leslieville, annexed 1884.

Seaton Village annexed 1888 (year from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Toronto). CAUTION: the bounding streets are the present-day neighbourhood limits from the Seaton Village article, not a stated annexation boundary.

north: Grand Trunk Railway lands and a line between Fermanagh Avenue and Wright Avenue
note: Village of Parkdale (487 acres, limits as incorporated 1879), annexed March 1889 (annexation year from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkdale,_Toronto).
